observations: A large rounded form fills most of the frame, lit from the upper left by white ray-like streaks against a warm orange-amber background; the surface mixes teal, gold, and dark brown.
A single dark circular socket near center contains a small white-ringed eye; to its right a second large hollow socket shows no visible eye, giving the face an asymmetric, off-balance quality.
A wide open mouth near the lower center shows a row of blocky white teeth rendered with short stacked marks; loose zigzag lines in white, red, and yellow run across the bulging cheek masses.
reading: Warm amber light rakes across a swollen, lumpen face from the upper left, catching teal and gold patches on otherwise dark surfaces. One eye stares back from a deep socket while the other sits empty, pulling the face off-balance. The open mouth and blocky teeth read as a shout or gasp. Zigzag lines layered over the rounded forms add a restless surface quality that sits against the stillness of the hollow socket.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits at the title-numbered end of the run. Its neighbor in both title order and recorded creation order is nifty faces #131, which uses a bright sky-blue field and a more upright face structure — a strong contrast to the amber darkness and asymmetry here.

connections.reason: nifty faces #131 shares the zigzag line overlay and visible teeth, but its open sky-blue ground and frontal face structure contrast sharply with the amber darkness and hollow socket of #132.

Scrimshaw 41 shows a wide-open mouth with a row of white tooth marks against a dark ground with warm amber patches — a cross-collection formal echo the collector links through shared tooth-and-darkness structure.

lookingQuestion: What does the difference between the filled eye socket and the empty one do to how you read the direction the face is turned?
ambiguities: The second large dark socket may contain a deeply shadowed form rather than being fully empty; image resolution makes this uncertain.
nnotb #203 was inspected and set aside — warm tones are shared but no strong formal overlap with this work justifies a connection.
